about: The sourced production rules (docs/SOURCED_RULES.md). Source types: A article/official page/study, B book, C YouTube video or vlog. binding = two or more types and enforced in code; hypothesis = one type, REVIEW only, the project's existing number; house = the creator's dated decision.

rules.statement: Heard pace is measured on the finished read: target 170 wpm, accepted 155-185; one band everywhere (five studies agree 170 is the YouTube norm; one source type, so the project's own number stays).

rules.statement: The first spoken sentence is the hook, in one of four forms YouTube names (a question, a cold-open incident line, a claim with a number, or a preview of what the viewer will see); never a greeting, the channel name, 'today we look at' or 'subscribe'. Branding, if any, comes after the hook.

rules.statement: A camera move on a still keeps its scale within 1.00-1.15 (a push at most 1.10 by default); accents (punch) are exempt but their stack never exceeds 1.15 x 1.18 (punch_max; a punch's strength is at most 1 in the schema). The blurred backdrop behind a dialogue close-up (production/faces.ZOOM) is a fixed framing behind the inset, not a camera move: this rule does not govern it.

rules.statement: No camera shake as a move (the creator's UR-13). A shake exists only as an accent on an impact beat (a blow, a fall, a collision, an explosion), decaying within 1.0 s, peak at most 7 % of frame height, never on a dialogue-only shot. The house shake (0.45 s, 1.8 % at strength 1) sits inside both caps.

rules.statement: Cut continuity: across a hard cut the hero or focal point stays within 10 % of the frame of its previous position unless the cut opens a new scene; the shot size changes by a full step (never the same framing of the same picture twice in a row); a direction change over 90 degrees needs a neutral picture between. Code checks the same framing (two zooms within same_framing_zoom_tol, an engineering tolerance); the focal shift and the direction change are the planner's (edit-planner, editing-style), because the script carries no focal point or screen direction per shot.

rules.statement: Section-aware rhythm: in the first 30 s something changes on screen at least every 5 s (FAIL); in the body a still longer than 20 s is REVIEW and longer than 40 s is FAIL; the average stays at most 10 pictures a minute (the creator) with one burst of 5-10 cuts allowed per 2-3 min; every change carries new information. A change is anything new on screen: a cut, a bubble, an accent (not the wobble), a data visual, a card or a visual beat (default of 2026-10-20: a beat counts; the creator may overturn it).

rules.statement: Visual-beat cadence while the narrator speaks (VB-01, production/beats.py). On production_script/3 pace follows new information: a narration stretch with nothing new on screen (a cut, bubble, accent, data visual, card or visual beat) longer than 8 s is REVIEW and longer than 15 s FAIL. On /2 the metronome: a beat about every 1.5 s, REVIEW over 2 s, FAIL over 3 s, a segment mean over 1.8 s REVIEW. A stricter, narration-only rule nested inside BP-40 (the whole video's still limits, counted on the same events): in the hook window BP-40's still limit is the stricter one, in the body this rule's FAIL is. Shorts follow BP-45 instead.

rules.statement: Motion variety (MO-02..MO-07, edit/motion_lint.py): every 60 s shows at least 3 kinds of visual event; at most 4 shots in a row are only a camera move; two pop or slam words at least 12 s apart; at least half of the shots move besides the camera; more than 3 shot holds in a row within 15 % of each other, or a segment of 5+ shots whose holds vary by under 0.2 of their mean, is a metronome. All REVIEW: the numbers are an engineering hypothesis (the sources back variance, not these values). MO-01's still limit is BP-40.

rules.statement: The Universal Rule Base shot plan (D-37, edit/shot_rules.py): shot lengths A 5-7 s, B 3.5-5 s, C 2.5-4 s (UR-11); in the first 30 s at least 6 shots, each within its minimum + 1 s (UR-02); a sound event by 1 s (UR-01); an A shot holds one zoom in 1.05-1.08, a C shot pulls from at most 1.08 (UR-13, inside BP-20); at most 10 % of the transitions are dissolves (UR-14, the hard-cut convention BP-31 names); a cut keeps 0.05 s from both words (UR-12); at most 15 % of the B shots faceless and a stakes line of at least 5 words (UR-16, UR-17). The hook's form is BP-03, not a question by 5 s.
